rationale:
`src/authoring/mod.rs#struct[PendingAssessment]` is the staging type between a valid judgment and its persistence. Its `subject` field determines the evidence destination, and its `record` field is the evidence JSON that gets written. A change to `requirements.authoring.persistence`, such as what is written or where, could require changing it. That makes `{cite}` appropriate.

An `{impl}` is not called for. The struct only holds data. The decisions the requirement states are made elsewhere, and those items carry their own `{impl}` references:
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]` (the code that marks the evidence as written)
- `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[stage_record]`
- `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[persist_record]`
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[record]`
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]`

The struct is reached from those marked items through the types they use, so it needs no `{impl}` of its own. It is not a test. The struct has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement, so the citation is not redundant.
